provenance.instrument: Lower Pottsgrove Township Zoning Ordinance of 1973 (Chapter 250 Zoning, Ord. No. 127 of 6-4-1973, reenacted 5-20-2010 by Ord. No. 294, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 LO2382, Township of Lower Pottsgrove, Montgomery County (the code home page names the county and the code names Sanatoga and the Pottsgrove School District). Chapter 250 Zoning was adopted 6-4-1973 by Ord. No. 127, reenacted 5-20-2010 by Ord. No. 294 and amended since, most recently by Ord. No. 373 (11-3-2025, village development in R-1), which is folded into the text. New Laws: none. Every district article sets its uses and figures in text. The only attachments are the zoning map, the map amendments and the sign types appendix
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360: 'Includes legislation through 08-03-2026.' New Laws: none
checks: The code's unit is 'Temporary living quarters for relatives or household employees', a use accessory to a dwelling, by special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board, in the house or in an approved accessory building (250-21B(4))

At most two persons may live in the quarters, the house must be owner-occupied, and the Board must be satisfied the unit will only be occupied by relatives or household employees of the owner (250-21B(4)(a) to (c))

A unit attached to the house keeps an internal connection, such as a stairway or corridor, and each unit has two means of access. Any new outside entrance faces the rear, and the house must still look like a single-family detached dwelling from the street and from other properties (250-21B(4)(d), (e), (i))

The owner records a deed restriction that bars selling the property as two or more dwelling units, and renews the zoning permit every year by showing the unit is still occupied by relatives or employees (250-21B(4)(f), (k))

A dwelling unit is a unit whose occupants 'do not live and eat with other persons' and that has direct outside access or its own kitchen (250-8). Whether the quarters count as a second dwelling unit for lot area per unit and parking is not settled

When relatives or employees no longer live there, an attached unit goes back into the house, a unit in an accessory building goes back to an accessory use or storage, and 'A detached modular unit shall be completely removed from the property' (250-21B(4)(g))

A new detached building meets the accessory setbacks and is separated from neighbors by substantial landscaping (250-21B(4)(i)). Accessory buildings may not stand closer to the street than the front of the house, need 20 ft to the rear line (the principal rear yard over 600 sq ft) and the principal side yard or the house's actual side yard, whichever is less restrictive (250-21D)

A detached accessory building over 600 sq ft, up to 1,000 sq ft, or over 21 ft tall needs its own special exception (250-21D(4)). In R-1, R-2 and the Preservation Subdivision District a building accessory to a dwelling may be at most 15 ft and one story (250-51B, 250-60, 250-73B). In R-3 no building may exceed 35 ft or two stories, whichever is greater (250-63G), so a detached building there may be up to 35 ft with that special exception above 21 ft

Every dwelling unit or other structure for residential occupancy needs at least 600 sq ft of habitable floor area, or 200 sq ft per person if more (250-28). A detached unit is then over 600 sq ft, so it takes the principal rear yard and needs the 250-21D(4) special exception
With an on-lot septic system the county health department must find it adequate for the added use. With public sewer the Township Authority decides whether more EDUs are needed (250-21B(4)(h))

A conversion of a single-family dwelling into a dwelling for two or more families is a special exception in every district, but only for 'a large dwelling with relatively little economic usefulness as a conforming use', with a petition signed by owners of 60% of the frontage on the street within 1,000 ft, and with each unit at least 600 sq ft (250-27)

A two-family dwelling (twin or duplex) is by right in R-3 (8,712 sq ft of lot per unit, public sewer) and in LCO and LC (250-62B, 250-63, 250-64A, 250-97J, 250-113E). R-4 takes the R-3 uses 'except duplexes permitted under § 250-62B', and 250-62B is the two-family dwelling listing, so whether a twin is allowed in R-4 is not settled (250-66A). 250-67A(1), B(1) and C(1) regulate two-family dwellings in R-4, which supports the reading that twins are allowed and only duplexes are excluded
In the Floodplain Conservation District only the listed uses are allowed, and accessory uses only 'excepting enclosed structures'. No dwelling use is listed (250-40)

In the Sanatoga Village District Overlay the front yard is 20 ft or the average of the neighbors, whichever is less, the side yard 15 ft, the rear yard 30 ft and the height 40 ft. The overlay 'shall supersede only the building setback, building scale, parking and sign regulations' of the base district (250-125B). Public sewer and water are required for conversions (250-126, 250-130, 250-131)
A lot of record too small for the district may be built on by special exception (250-14) or by variance (250-208A). No section read bars a use variance
Parking is 2 spaces per dwelling unit for a single-family dwelling (Table 250-202). The code calls the quarters an accessory dwelling unit in 250-21B(4)(d), so it may need 2 more
No dwelling may be erected or altered unless it has direct access through an open space on the lot to a public street (250-19)

In LCO multifamily dwellings are by right (250-97K), a mixed-use building may hold up to two dwelling units (250-97L), and a conversion meets the district rules 'to the maximum extent feasible' with parking cut by up to 40% (250-111). LC permits every LCO use (250-113E, 250-123)
A use of the same general character as a listed use is a special exception in CO (250-87N(1)) and a conditional use in LCO (250-98B) and LC (250-114B)
Impervious cover in R-2, R-3 and R-4 depends on lot size: 35% under 10,000 sq ft, 30% from 10,001 to 29,999 sq ft, 25% at 30,000 sq ft or more (250-59E, 250-63C(2), 250-67C(2)(b))
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Lower Pottsgrove Township, Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360, one page at a time, on 2026-11-16, mostly in print view. Read: 250-7 and 250-8 (definitions), Article III, Article IV through 250-33K, Articles V to XI, XIII to XVII, XIX, XXIB, XXVIII, the use list and figures of Articles XII, XX, XXIA and XXII (through the page's text tree), Table 250-202, 250-221 to 250-228 and the New Laws page. Searched G-IN and the Planned Mixed-Use Development overlay for dwelling uses. Not read: Article XXIV (Q), Article XXV (airport overlay), Article XXVI (signs), 250-33L to 250-36 (steep slopes, antennas, lighting), the rest of Articles XXI, XXIA and XXIII, Article XXIX and XXXI to XXXII. The code search was run for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, family member, living quarters, ECHO, guest house, tenant house, caretaker, conversion, second dwelling, carriage house, granny, accessory suite, relative, servant and quarters. A dwelling is a unit with direct outside access or its own kitchen (250-8). Coverage is the share of a site occupied by buildings and impervious coverage is defined separately (250-8). Density is the developable area divided by the district minimum lot size (250-8 'Developable area' C). Impervious coverage in R-2, R-3 and R-4 depends on lot size: 35% under 10,000 sq ft, 30% from 10,001 to 29,999 sq ft, 25% at 30,000 sq ft or more (250-59E, 250-63C(2), 250-67C(2)(b)). The base rows store 30%, the figure for the district minimum lot with public sewer and water, and max_impervious_by_lot_size gives all three tiers, which the lot fit uses. The R-2 rows without both services (30,000 sq ft and more) store 25%. The tables give no figure for a lot of exactly 10,000 sq ft. The airport overlay, PMUD (40 acres) and GRO (15 acres) were read and do not change the file. A family is related persons or a community living arrangement (250-8). 250-8 defines a dwelling unit as one whose occupants 'do not live and eat with other persons'.

value.name: Conversion to a dwelling for two families (R-1, PSD, LCO, LC)
value.conditions: The Zoning Hearing Board may allow the conversion of a single-family dwelling or other building into a dwelling for two or more families. A petition in favor signed by owners of 60% or more of the frontage on the same street within 1,000 ft. Each unit at least 600 sq ft, plus 100 sq ft for each bedroom over one. Lot area per family not less than 75% of the district requirement. Outside stairways enclosed and to the rear where practicable, two means of egress for each unit. Off-street parking met. The Board sets the number of families (250-27). In LCO and LC a conversion meets the district rules 'to the maximum extent feasible', and parking may be cut by up to 40% (250-111, 250-123)

disputed_by.note: The text speaks of 'the principal dwelling' and does not name the house type. Only (i), on exterior changes for an attached unit, names a single-family detached dwelling

value.condition: A unit attached to the house keeps an internal connection, such as a stairway or corridor, and each unit has two means of access. Any new outside entrance is to the rear, and the house keeps its appearance as a single-family detached dwelling.

A new detached building meets the accessory setbacks and is separated from adjacent properties by substantial landscaping. When no longer used by relatives or employees, a unit in an accessory building returns to an accessory use or storage, and a detached modular unit is removed.
A deed restriction bars selling the property as two or more dwelling units. An attached unit returns to the house when it is no longer used by relatives or employees.
An on-lot septic system must be found adequate by the county health department for the added use. With public sewer the Township Authority decides whether more EDUs are needed.

In the Floodplain Conservation District only the listed uses are allowed. They include no dwelling, and accessory uses only 'excepting enclosed structures'. In the floodway no construction of any kind is allowed unless its effect on flood heights is fully offset.

In the Sanatoga Village District Overlay the front yard is at least 20 ft from the ultimate right-of-way or the average of the neighbors, whichever is less, the side yard 15 ft and the rear yard 30 ft, and buildings may be 40 ft tall. Parking may not be in the front yard. The overlay replaces only the base district's setback, building scale, parking and sign rules. Uses, lot sizes and impervious cover stay those of the base district.

A lot in an approved cluster development or village development follows that plan's lot and yard figures (R-1 cluster 12,000 sq ft lots, R-2 cluster 10,000 sq ft, R-3 cluster 8,000 sq ft, village development 6,000 sq ft). In a village development accessory structures are not permitted.

Every dwelling unit needs at least 600 sq ft of habitable floor area. A detached unit is then a detached accessory building over 600 sq ft: it needs its own special exception under 250-21D(4), may be at most 1,000 sq ft, and takes the district's rear yard for a principal building.
